feed.title: Lupine Science
feed.subtitle: Lupine Science measures where machine-learned models of atoms go wrong, against published references and pass/fail gates set in advance, and publishes every verdict, failures included.

entry.title: Learning What an Error Pattern Can Tell Us
entry.summary: A retrospective analysis of previously examined data: errors stayed concentrated, but a learned shared direction added little or no advantage over a simple common-direction baseline. Also: where model disagreement helped, and a diffusion correction that reaches its limit. No new physical validation is claimed.

entry.title: Lupine Science is heading to TMS2027
entry.summary: A poster abstract was accepted for TMS2027 (Orlando, 14–18 March 2027). It is a conference presentation, not a paper. The accepted abstract described a universal error "hyper-ribbon"; our record no longer supports that, and the proceedings manuscript replaces it with narrower measurement claims.

entry.title: What the Cap Was Hiding
entry.summary: A preregistered correction trial (Round 4, July 2026) failed. Going back through the mathematics showed four defects, none of them in the physics: the gate that decided when a correction could act was mis-tuned, the confirmatory test could not have passed even with a perfect result, a proposed input statistic measured only the panel's bookkeeping, and the replacement gate has a rounding hazard of its own. The clearance conditions are Lean 4 theorems; the rest is arithmetic replayed from the hash-locked records.

entry.title: Shared DFT Anchors: A Projected Saving, and What Happened When We Ran It
entry.summary: Projected accounting, no new DFT: 154 instead of 558 projected DFT evaluations on 29 analyzable paths (72.4% fewer DFT evaluations, projected). The baseline is four separate runs; paths have 5–7 images, so the union covers most images and deduplication alone caps the saving near 73%. When we ran the pilot, it was about 700 meV off the published references; see "What happened when we ran it".

entry.title: The Small Cell Held: A 16-Element MLIP Elastic Benchmark
entry.summary: On a 16-metal panel, 1×1×1 TensorNet/PBE cells matched 3×3×3 cells for elastic-constant error (14.55 vs 14.61 GPa MAE), while a global correction made the result worse (63.40 GPa).

entry.title: The Savings Stack: A Booklet on Compute Savings in Atomistic Simulation
entry.summary: The Savings Stack v1 (July 2026): a 16-page booklet on compute savings in atomistic simulation, with a hashable data pack. Its headline count is projected, not measured: four models sharing anchors would need 154 instead of 558 DFT evaluations on 29 short paths (72.4% fewer, against a baseline of four separate runs), and no new DFT was run. When the pilot was later run, it was about 700 meV off the published references.

entry.title: A Seven-Tier Map of MLIP Error, by Property Type (July 2026)
entry.summary: A July 2026 map of MLIP error by property type, from lattice constants to magnetism: where a correction has held in a narrow, stated case, where only boundary results apply, and where the honest answer is abstention. Later results that changed the map are dated in the body.

entry.title: The Z1 Barrier Panel: 42 Li-ion Migration Paths from a Published DFT-NEB Benchmark
entry.summary: Our barrier campaigns run on 42 published Li-ion migration paths from the LiTraj nebDFT2k benchmark: 30 frozen test paths and 12 disjoint training paths. In Round 4, four foundation MLIPs missed a 40 meV gate on the test panel; in Round 5, a direction-gated correction abstained for all four models, so none was applied.

entry.title: Round 4: Three Failures and One Abstention, Preregistered
entry.summary: In four preregistered campaigns in July 2026 (Round 4), no gate passed: three failed and one abstained. MACE-MP-0 small and medium, MACE-MPA-0 medium and CHGNet missed a 40 meV migration-barrier gate (MAE 135.0–242.5 meV on completed paths); a lattice- and elastic-constant correction on rocksalt ionics and perovskites failed; every selected Δ-correction made catalyst-adsorption holdout error worse; and the magnetism campaign abstained. Each result is hash-locked, including our own preregistration violations.

entry.title: Beyond Carbon: The Error Geometry of Environmental Materials
entry.summary: The opening piece of a July 2026 series on environmental materials. It argues that their useful chemistry happens in under-coordinated environments, where machine-learned potentials are least reliable, and sets out what we would need to test. A direction, not a result.

entry.title: Cement, Concrete, and the Weight of the Built World
entry.summary: Cement decarbonization depends on disordered, metastable, under-coordinated phases, which are where machine-learned potentials are least reliable. This July 2026 piece sets out where measured model error matters for alternative binders, clinkers and CO₂-cured concrete, and what has been tested so far. A direction, not a result.

entry.title: Critical Minerals, PFAS, and the Remediation Imperative
entry.summary: Critical-mineral recycling, direct lithium extraction and PFAS destruction share a materials-discovery problem: binding and activation energies in under-coordinated environments, where machine-learned potentials are least reliable. This piece describes where the work is aimed and what has been tested so far. A direction, not a result.

entry.title: Methane and Refrigerants: Cutting the Non-CO₂ Climate Forcers
entry.summary: Methane and hydrofluorocarbon refrigerants are large non-CO₂ climate levers, and both are materials-limited. This July 2026 piece sets out where measured model error matters for their discovery and what would have to be tested before a fast screen could be trusted. A direction, not a result.

entry.title: Water and Air: The Materials Behind What We Drink and Breathe
entry.summary: Water and air quality depend on materials that separate and transform molecules in under-coordinated environments, where machine-learned potentials are least reliable. This July 2026 piece sets out where a measured correction might help and what would have to be tested first. A direction, not a result.

entry.title: The Correction That Hurt, and the Claim We Narrowed
entry.summary: Our first correction made alloy predictions worse. We turned that failure into a Lean-checked rule about correction direction, explored a direction-gated rule that cut lattice errors in-sample, and registered a kill condition for Round 3. It fired, and we narrowed the claim to same-class lattice constants. Round 4's preregistered test of that lattice result then failed, so the claim is not established.

entry.title: LUPI Gains HFC Refrigerant Research Payloads
entry.summary: A LUPI viewer release (July 2026) adds R32 and R125 NVT simulations from the Maginn group force fields, a fix ave/chunk profile parser, vector glyph views and level-of-detail rendering for large scenes.

entry.title: Five Materials Worth Getting Right: Cathodes, Electrolytes, Sorbents, Catalysts and Absorbers
entry.summary: Five climate-relevant material classes whose performance depends on defects, surfaces and transition states, where machine-learned potentials are least reliable. This July 2026 piece describes the targets, the literature on why they matter, and what we have tested so far. A direction, not a result; it makes no climate-impact claim of its own.

entry.title: From Predicted Crystal to Commercial Cell
entry.summary: A predicted crystal passes through synthesis, coating, cell fabrication, characterization, integration and manufacturing before it becomes a product. This July 2026 piece, rewritten in November 2026, maps those hand-offs by type of organisation for batteries, carbon removal, ammonia and solar absorbers, and says where knowing a model's error would help. A direction, not a result.

entry.title: The 0.2% Synthesis Problem
entry.summary: A literature review: of 380,000 structures GNoME reported as computationally stable, 736 had been independently synthesized by late 2023 (about 0.2%). It describes four structural filters between a predicted crystal and a made material and the questions they raise for climate-relevant materials. A direction, not a result.

entry.title: The Trust Layer
entry.summary: Our founding thesis, July 2026. AI made proposing and simulating materials cheap; deciding which predictions to believe is now the bottleneck. We think independent, preregistered measurement of model error is the missing piece, and we publish it in the open. A direction, not a result.

entry.title: A smooth, environment-resolved error field behind uMLIP errors on fcc metals
entry.summary: For nine fcc metals, an error field fitted to three other observables predicted the never-fitted (110) surface-energy error of four foundation MLIPs at r = 0.906 across 36 model–material cells (material-clustered 95% CI 0.82–0.96; permutation null centred near 0.44; significant for three of the four models). Used as an energy-only correction beside CHGNet, the field cut blind (110) surface-energy error from 9.7% to 1.5% on nickel and from 28.0% to 13.7% on copper: one model, two metals, one facet.

entry.title: The Order Is Right, the Size Is Wrong
entry.summary: Across 21 materials and 228 published reference values, four foundation MLIPs ranked surface energies almost correctly (Spearman 0.88–1.00) while missing magnitudes by tens of percent. Apparent cross-model alignment sat inside a coupling-aware null, so we do not count it as a result.

entry.title: Why LUPI?
entry.summary: LUPI as a live, install-free window into molecular structures and its implications for research, teaching, and public trust.

entry.title: Why Lupine Science?
entry.summary: Our June 2026 launch essay, revised. Generative AI produces far more material candidates than labs can test, and the simulations used to rank them are wrong in structured ways. We set out to measure those errors before a lab commits to a candidate. A direction, not a result.

entry.title: From Fantasy Frameworks to Makeable Materials: A Prospectus for Formalized MOF Discovery
entry.summary: A June 2026 proposal: encode the rules of MOF assembly, stability and synthesis as stated assumptions in Lean, so that each AI-generated candidate carries an explicit, checked list of the assumptions it meets, and test those rules against a lab's successes and failures. A direction, not a result; nothing in it has been built or tested.
